newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: MOZAMBIQUE EXPECTS BIGGER 1997 COTTON CROP.
newsitem.headline: MOZAMBIQUE EXPECTS BIGGER 1997 COTTON CROP.

text.p: Mozambique's total raw cotton production has almost doubled since 1989, the National Cotton Institute said in its latest report on Friday.
The institute said the southern African country's seed cotton production was expected to reach 55,000 tonnes this year, compared to 28,000 tonnes in 1989.
It said the total 1997 production of cotton fibre, after ginning, was expected to be 18,000 tonnes.

The Lonrho Mozambique Agricultural Company, one of the country's cotton growers, said in a report released this week it and other cotton industry players had produced a total of 51,000 tonnes of seed cotton last year.
In 1996 Mozambique exported 13,528 tonnes of cotton fibre, valued at $15.7 million, while 1,802 tonnes was supplied to the national textile industry.
Mozambique's peak for seed cotton production was 144,000 tonnes in 1973.
Cotton production in Mozambique has been growing steadily since the creation of mixed economy of state and private companies in 1990.
It had declined after independence from Portugal in 1975.
Cotton is currently Mozambique's second biggest export revenue earner, after cashew nuts.
